title: Increase me in knowledge
hookLine: say, my Lord, increase me in knowledge (20:114)

lines: THE PEN AHEAD OF THE MIND.
cards: A student in the front row writes so fast to catch every word that half of what's said slips past. The pen is ahead of the understanding.

The commentators, drawing on a hadith, describe something like it in the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: when the angel Jibril brought a passage, he would repeat each word as it came, hurrying, afraid of losing one.
Ta-Ha has a verse for that moment. It tells him not to hurry, and then gives him words to ask with.

teach.b: Verse one hundred fourteen begins with praise: exalted is God, the true King. Then: don't hurry with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is complete.
Al-Qiyamah says it more vividly: don't move your tongue to rush it; We will gather it and recite it for you. The knowledge is safe; you can breathe.
And then, in Pickthall's words: "and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge." In Arabic: rabbi zidni 'ilma.
Some commentators count this as the one place in the Qur'an where the Prophet is told to ask for more of something.
Not more wealth, not more time, not more followers. More knowledge. And 'ilm in the Qur'an is wide.
It's knowledge of God first, but it also takes in understanding, discernment, knowing how things work and how to live. Tradition says the first word revealed to him was iqra': read, recite.
Here, years later, the request is: more.

A hadith in Ibn Majah and Tirmidhi preserves a prayer of his that builds on the verse: he asked God to make what he'd learned useful, to teach him what would be useful, and to increase him in knowledge.

teach.h: MY LORD! INCREASE ME IN KNOWLEDGE.
teach.b: That's the balance: don't rush what's coming, and keep asking for more. Some Muslim students say rabbi zidni 'ilma before they study, before an exam, before opening a book. Six words in English.

how: Muslims say rabbi zidni 'ilma, from 20:114, before studying, teaching or exams, and it can be seen written up in classrooms in Muslim communities.

games.q: the angel is reciting, and you're repeating every word as fast as you can, afraid you'll forget. what does the verse tell you?
o: don't hurry; and say, my Lord, increase me in knowledge.
ask the angel to slow down.
games.why: don't rush the revelation before it's complete, and ask for more knowledge (20:114).

practice: Think of something you don't know but would like to: a word in another language, how an engine works, the name of the tree outside your window, the meaning of a verse you've heard all your life.
Choose one, and hold the wish to understand it, without rushing, the way the verse asks. If you pray, you can say rabbi zidni 'ilma, my Lord, increase me in knowledge.

wordCard.voice: 'Ilm. Knowledge, wide in the Qur'an: the Prophet was told in Ta-Ha to ask his Lord for more of it. Today's word.
